Zyven

A language model built from the ground up

Zyven is a small language model trained from scratch by Nnamdi Chidume. It runs on PyTensorForge, a machine learning framework he wrote himself: the tensors, the tokenizer, the transformer, the training loop and the server answering you right now are all his code, built on NumPy.

How Zyven was made

  1. TokenizerA byte-level BPE tokenizer, trained on the pretraining text with special tokens for chat turns.
  2. PretrainingA decoder-only GPT model learns language from public story and educational text.
  3. Chat fine-tuningThe model is trained on conversations, learning only from the assistant's replies.
  4. ServingThe exported model streams replies through PyTensorForge's OpenAI-compatible server, with a KV cache for fast generation.

The creator

Nnamdi Chidume

Machine-level engineer. Creator of the Ardan programming language.

Nnamdi is a full-stack and iOS engineer with more than nine years of experience building web and mobile products. He likes to understand software all the way down, so he also builds the systems most developers only use: a programming language, a browser engine, a database engine, JavaScript and machine learning frameworks, and the model behind this chat. He shares what he learns on his YouTube channel, Understanding Dev, and on Medium.
